conventions.convention: Lengths start at n=0; a zero-qubit register is C with basis {1}. Output tuples have distinct ordered wires and may be empty. Auxiliary initialization does not require restoration.
The root inner product is linear first and conjugate-linear second. Acceptance sums squared coordinate moduli over every unmeasured wire.

Full-list uniformity means one polynomial-time deterministic one-tape machine prints the complete circuit from unary length. Input and total-wire counts are unary; gates are exactly H, T, T†, and control-first CNOT.
YES and NO sets are disjoint; off-promise behavior is unrestricted. The total polynomial-time terminal predicate receives both classical input x and measured output z.

Clean and dirty counts require declared exact return contracts for a specified data/ancilla partition and target unitary. Zero initialization alone supplies neither contract. Minimum-layer depth differs from declared depth.

Oracle ports are fixed memoryless unitaries. Forward, inverse, controlled-forward, and controlled-inverse access require separate grants. Raw calls and positive charged query costs are separate; binary charges can be exponentially large.
For δ=u/v, repetition uses r=2s(n)^2(ell(v)+1); ties at the rational midpoint are accepted. Only computational-basis inputs are copied.

load_bearing.statement: A finite quantum promise computation consists of a disjoint promise pair, finite unitary circuits on classical-basis inputs with zero-initialized auxiliary wires, distinct ordered output-wire tuples, and total terminal predicates; no intermediate measurement or off-promise correctness requirement is imposed.

A full-list uniform quantum circuit family is a sequence (C_n) for n≥0 together with one fixed deterministic one-tape Turing machine G and constants c≥1 and k∈N such that G, on unary input 1^n, halts within c(n+1)^k transitions with a valid complete circuit description on its final tape.

For every finite promise computation, every length n, and every classical input x of length n, the output weights are nonnegative and sum to one. Acceptance is the probability of the specified acceptance event, lies in [0,1], and agrees with the computational-basis POVM outcome law on the named output register.

The cost record separates complete-description length, gate count, minimum-layer depth, width, declared exact clean/dirty ancilla counts, generator time, predicate time and space, named oracle queries, and applicable precision data; inapplicable coordinates are marked not applicable.

Under the algorithm's valid-input conditions and base YES acceptance at least α(n) and NO acceptance at most β(n), with α(n)−β(n)≥1/s(n), amplified YES acceptance is at least 1−δ(n) and NO acceptance at most δ(n). The repeated gate count is r(n)g(C_n)+n(r(n)−1), width is r(n)w(C_n), and depth, description length, generation time, and predicate time and space are polynomial.

A promise problem belongs to BQP in the QC14 model when a full-list uniform fixed-library family and polynomial-time acceptance predicate have acceptance at least 2/3 on every YES input and at most 1/3 on every NO input, without off-promise conditions.

concerns.concern: The Statement says, 'Whenever the base interface declares clean or dirty ancillary registers satisfying the corresponding exact contract, each such register's count is multiplied by r(n).' Proof 4.1 asserts preservation without requiring these registers to avoid the first n input wires. The cited cost definition permits an arbitrary declared data/ancilla partition. At n=1 take the gate-free identity circuit on one input wire, declare D empty and that wire A, with target I_C. Its exact dirty contract holds. Choose output wire 0, YES={1}, NO={0}, α=2/3, β=1/3, s=3, δ=1/4, giving r=72. The repeated circuit is the input-copy CNOT fanout. On the purported repeated dirty register it maps |1,0,...,0> to |1,1,...,1>, so it is not I and does not satisfy the asserted repeated dirty contract. The probability amplification remains valid; the ancillary-contract conclusion needs an explicit restriction or a separate treatment of partitions intersecting input wires.

alerts.finding: F2 states, '[[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]: the fixed inter-query circuits do not depend on the oracle input; the output is a measured computational-basis bit.' That supplier defines ordinary H/T/T†/CNOT full-list families, contains no oracle-query interface, and permits arbitrary ordered output tuples. It does not state either attributed query-model condition. Proof 1.1 uses the input-independence assertion and Proof 2.1 uses the output-bit interpretation. These are standard query-model assumptions, but their stated citation does not supply them.

F8 states, '[[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-promise-problem]]: the query algorithm is input-independent between oracle calls and must meet its error guarantee on every input in the full Boolean-cube promise.' The promise supplier supports the correctness scope, but def-qc-uniform-circuit-family defines an ordinary finite-gate family and supplies no hidden-instance oracle-query independence condition. Proof 1.2 and 4.1 invoke F8. The oracle-query condition needs the actual query/access interface rather than this attribution.

The Definition calls A_n 'a clean-ancilla register' and subsequently says only that 'the clean ancillas start in |0^{a(n)}>.' Its cited def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas defines clean ancillas by exact return to zero for every data vector, while def-qc-promise-computation-model explicitly distinguishes initialization from that stronger contract. This verifier definition imposes no return condition. The term 'clean' therefore attributes a contract not supplied by the displayed interface; zero-initialized workspace is the property actually stated.
